info.name: KSA Islamic Financing Platform
info.description:
Complete API collection for the KSA Islamic Financing Platform.

All API requests go through Kong API Gateway (port 8000).
URL pattern: {{kongUrl}}/{service-name}/api/v1/...
Kong strips the /{service-name} prefix before forwarding.

Routing:
  /onboarding-service/*       -> onboarding-workflow-service:8089
  /identity-service/*          -> identity-service:8083
  /kyc-adapter-service/*       -> kyc-adapter-service:8087
  /customer-service/*          -> customer-service:8084
  /global-profile-service/*    -> global-profile-service:8085
  /pii-vault-service/*         -> pii-vault-service:8086
  /wallet-service/*            -> wallet-service:8088
  /risk-service/*              -> risk-service:8090
  /product-service/*           -> product-service:8091
  /lending-service/*           -> lending-service:8092
  /middleware-third-party/*   -> middleware-third-party:8093

Services (12):
  1. Identity Service      — Auth, Keycloak, RBAC (login, register, PIN login)
  2. Onboarding Service    — 8-step signal-driven Temporal workflow
  3. KYC Adapter Service   — Nafath, Yakeen, Simah, OTP, Sanctions
  4. Customer Service      — CIF, lifecycle, employment, bank accounts, EDD reference data
  5. Global Profile Service — Zero-PII global UID, regional profiles, PII access tokens
  6. PII Vault Service     — Encrypted PII storage (AES-256-GCM), GDPR erasure
  7. Wallet Service        — SAR digital wallet, top-up
  8. Risk Service          — Internal checks, AML/CFT risk scoring (EastNets model), credit scoring engine, blacklist mgmt
  9. Product Service       — Islamic financing product catalog (5-step wizard, 8 settings tabs)
  10. Lending Service      — Islamic loan origination, Temporal SAGA workflow, Murabaha/Ijara/Tawarruq
  11. Middleware Third Party — Centralized third-party API management (18 providers, ~80 APIs)

Onboarding Flow:
  1. Initiate Onboarding (public) -> get workflowId
  2. Verify OTP (public) -> get JWT tokens
  3. Accept Terms (JWT)
  4. Initiate Nafath (JWT) -> get randomNumber
  5. Nafath Callback (public webhook)
  6. Submit Additional Info (JWT) — isPep: true -> EDD required
  6b. Submit EDD Form (JWT, PEP path only)
  6c. AML Risk Scoring (auto) — calls risk-service weighted scoring engine
  6d. Risk Decision (auto) — APPROVE/HOLD/BLOCK
  7. Set App PIN (JWT) — 6-digit PIN
  8. Check Status (JWT) -> full workflow state (includes amlRiskLevel, amlTotalScore)

Device metadata headers: X-Device-Id, X-Latitude, X-Longitude, X-Client-Ip, X-User-Agent
All endpoints use nationalId. workflowId = onboarding-{nationalId}.
Variables auto-set by test scripts after Initiate and Verify OTP steps.

request.description:
Kong -> identity-service:8083
REQUIRES: Bearer token (accessToken)

Logs out the currently authenticated user by revoking ALL their active Keycloak sessions.

How it works:
  1. JWT sub claim se Keycloak user ID nikalta hai

  3. Keycloak ke tamam active sessions revoke ho jaate hain

item.name: 3 - Identity Service (identity-service)
item.description:
Kong -> identity-service:8083
URL: {{kongUrl}}/identity-service/api/v1/...

Identity Service: authentication, jCasbin RBAC authorization, role/permission/policy management.

RBAC Architecture:
  - Casbin enforcer with DB-backed policies (casbin_rule table)
  - CasbinAuthorizationFilter in Spring Security filter chain
  - Policy format: (role, obj, act) — obj+act model
  - @SecuredEndpoint annotation on all protected endpoints

Seeded Roles: super_admin, admin, csa, compliance_officer, underwriter, product_admin, partner_admin, head_of_accounts, customer
Seeded Policies: obj+act policies across 9 role tiers

Auth endpoints: register, onboarding-register, login, login-with-pin, SSO (PKCE), refresh, logout

item.description:

These are NOT REST endpoints — they interact directly with Temporal.
Use these to send signals to running workflows or query their state.

For now, documented as reference for how signals are sent programmatically.

request.description:
Send 'documents verified' signal to the running Temporal workflow.

This unblocks Step 3 (Document Verification) of the SAGA workflow.
The workflow waits up to 72 hours for this signal.

Set verified=true to approve, verified=false to reject documents.
If rejected, the workflow will compensate (cancel application).

Note: This endpoint needs to be implemented in the controller.
Currently the signal is sent programmatically via Temporal WorkflowClient.

Send 'documents rejected' signal to the running Temporal workflow.

This rejects the documents at Step 3, causing SAGA compensation.
The application will be CANCELLED.

Note: This endpoint needs to be implemented in the controller.

Send 'manual approval' signal to the running Temporal workflow.

This unblocks Step 7 (Approval Decision) of the SAGA workflow.
The workflow waits up to 7 days for this signal.

Approved amount/tenure/rate can override the requested values.
If not provided, the original requested values are used.

After approval, the workflow automatically:
  - Processes the approval (updates application)
  - Creates the loan record
  - Returns final LoanApplicationResult

  - currentStage: INITIATED | CREATING_APPLICATION | SUBMITTING | DOCUMENTS_PENDING | CREDIT_CHECK | SHARIA_VALIDATION | PROFIT_CALCULATION | PENDING_APPROVAL | CREATING_LOAN | COMPLETED | FAILED
  - applicationStatus: DRAFT | SUBMITTED | DOCUMENTS_PENDING | CREDIT_CHECK | SHARIA_VALIDATION | PENDING_APPROVAL | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED

This uses Temporal Query methods (synchronous, no side effects).

item.name: Eligibility (proxied from risk-service)
item.description:
Eligibility field definitions and evaluation — proxied from risk-service.

Risk-service is the single source of truth for:
  - Credit scoring field definitions (40+ seeded fields)
  - Product-specific criteria and rules
  - Eligibility evaluation (decision engine)

Lending-service proxies these endpoints so the mobile app uses a single base URL.

Flow:
  1. GET /eligibility-fields/product/{productId} → returns dynamic form fields
  2. Customer fills the form
  3. POST /loan-applications/initiate with eligibilityAnswers → lending-service calls risk-service evaluate
  4. Risk-service returns scoring result (eligible/not, score, details)

item.name: [lending] Get Eligibility Fields for Product (proxy → risk-service)

request.description:
Proxied from risk-service — Returns credit scoring field definitions for the product.
These are dynamic eligibility questions the mobile app renders.

Risk-service endpoint: GET /api/v1/risk/credit-scoring/products/{productId}/fields

Response: List of field definitions with fieldKey, nameEn, nameAr, dataType, active, sortOrder.
The mobile app uses field_key as the answer key when posting eligibility answers.

ELIGIBILITY_CHECK mode — Checks eligibility WITHOUT starting a loan workflow.

Lending-service forwards eligibilityAnswers to risk-service's decision engine:
  POST risk-service/api/v1/risk/credit-scoring/products/{productId}/evaluate

Response includes:
  - status: ELIGIBILITY_CHECKED
  - preQualification: { eligible, totalScore, maxPossibleScore, scorePercentage, details[] }
  - message: eligibility result summary

No workflowId or applicationId is created.

APPLY mode — Evaluates eligibility via risk-service decision engine, then starts Temporal workflow.

Flow:
  1. Lending-service calls risk-service evaluate with eligibilityAnswers
  2. If eligible=false → returns ELIGIBILITY_FAILED (no workflow started)
  3. If eligible=true → starts Temporal LoanApplicationWorkflow
  4. Returns workflowId, applicationId, preQualification result

Risk-service scoring:
  - Evaluates answers against product-specific criteria and rules
  - Returns eligible/not based on scored weight percentage vs minimum pass threshold
